18.t: Working with data: keeping it hot
q: Which jacket kept the water hottest in Test 1?
Calculate the mean for aluminium foil.
Identify the anomalous result, and calculate the bubble wrap mean without it.
47 °C in Test 3 is anomalous. Mean of 67 and 69 = 68 °C.
Explain why wool and bubble wrap insulate well.
Both trap air, a poor conductor, in small pockets so it cannot move and carry energy by convection.
A student says foil works because it stops conduction. Evaluate this claim.
Foil is a metal, a good conductor, so it does not stop conduction. It helps mainly by reflecting infrared radiation back and stopping some evaporation; it was only 5 °C better than no jacket.
